creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Follow on from `make-interaction` (a_25Rcu1uOI). Reproduced against v0.11.0.

Re-asking until a value is valid is a common shape:

```rad
env = ""
while env not in ["prod", "staging"]:
    env = input("Environment? ")   // line 8
```

`--reply 8:dev` reports:

> The input "Environment? " ran out of answers - it executed more times than `--reply` accounted for. Repeat the flag once per pass; rad won't reuse the last answer

True, and useless. The value was rejected and the loop came back around. Following the advice literally can never work - `--reply 8:dev --reply 8:dev` fails identically - so an agent keeps adding flags and keeps failing.

### Direction

rad can't distinguish "re-asked because the value was rejected" from "legitimately runs N times", but it doesn't have to. The message just needs to stop asserting one of them. Carrying both diagnoses is enough:

> ... ran out of answers after 1 pass. If the script re-asks until a value is accepted, more `--reply` flags won't help - check the value is one it takes.

Wording is the whole card; prompt-engineer principles apply, and RAD20047 is already dense.
title: RAD20047 blames the answer count when the answer was just rejected
